answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The garden report exposes the merge explicitly at each copper. Because of that, a hostile operator who spins up 263 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 292 times the capital for one share. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
